records.name: Friends of Vernon Park
records.summary: Neighbors in Germantown who clean, green, and look after Vernon Park. They also run park programs and hold open meetings each month.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer to clean, plant, and look after the park, help run community programs, or give money or skills. Anyone can come to the open monthly meeting.

schedule.text: Open monthly meetings on the third Monday, 6 to 7 pm. Held on Zoom in cold or bad weather and in the park in warmer months. Listed upcoming dates: Sept 21, Oct 19, Nov 23, and Dec 21 (2026).

cost.text: Not stated. The group welcomes gifts of time, skills, and money.

first_step.how: Come to the next open monthly meeting (third Monday, 6 to 7 pm, on Zoom or in the park), or email info@friendsofvernonpark.org to ask how to volunteer
first_step.basis: Meetings are open monthly and the site gives an email address for questions about joining

records.notes: The site posts no exact dates. The newest dated item is an open letter labeled September 2026, and a 2026 community bazaar is listed without a date. The address comes from the City list because the group's site does not publish one. Partners named on the site, not checked (no links captured): Black Writers Museum, Center in the Park, Fairmount Park Conservancy, and Philadelphia Parks and Recreation.

records.name: Friends of Weccacoe Playground
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Weccacoe Playground in Queen Village. They keep the playground in shape, help with cleanups, and coordinate tennis programs with the South Philly Tennis Association.
records.what_you_do: Help maintain the playground and its equipment, join cleanup days, and take turns with neighbors who open the gates in the morning and close them at night. Ask about the weekly community tennis and lessons.

schedule.text: Weekly community tennis and group lessons, run with the South Philly Tennis Association. The page gives no days or times.

first_step.how: Email weccacoe@qvna.org to ask about joining the Friends group, helping with cleanups, or the nightly lock and morning unlock
first_step.basis: The page gives a direct email for questions but no meeting time

records.notes: The page has no dated items. Its only date is in an image filename, which does not count as evidence, so the status rests on a working page with no dates. The group sits under the Queen Village Neighbors Association, which also gives info@qvna.org for access questions. Partners named on the page, not checked (no links captured): Courtyard Mentoring network and South Philly Tennis Association. Mother Bethel A.M.E. Church appears only as the historical seller of the land, not as a current partner.

records.name: Friends of Wissahickon Neighbors Park
records.summary: Volunteers who help look after Wissahickon Neighbors Park, run as a Friends section of the Wissahickon Neighbors Civic Association. The civic association's site invites people to volunteer at the park but does not describe the tasks.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for park volunteer opportunities listed on the civic association's park updates page. The site does not describe specific tasks.

cost.text: Not stated for the park group. The civic association takes membership and donations.

first_step.how: Use the civic association's Join page or Contact Us page to ask how to sign up for park volunteer days
first_step.basis: The way in runs through the civic association's membership, and the site does not say whether dues apply or whether meetings are open to all

records.notes: Shares a park and address with lead city_friends:854, which is marked duplicate. The email comes from the City list entry for lead 854; the City entry for this lead gives the stewardship office, which is not used. The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active under the rule for working sites without dates. The homepage shows no email. Civic association meetings are at Pilgrims Church, 3815 Terrace St, at 7 pm on the third Thursday of each month; that is the association's meeting, not a park group event. Partner logos were inferred from URLs only and not checked. Roxborough Development Corporation and Pilgrims Philly are organizations, not Friends groups, and were dropped.

records.name: Friends of the Wissahickon
records.summary: The Friends of the Wissahickon look after the 2,000-acre Wissahickon Valley Park through volunteer work, trail care, and guided hikes. Volunteers do the hands-on stewardship, and Trail Ambassadors lead the hikes.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer service day (planting and cleanups are listed), take on individual stewardship work, join a corporate or youth crew, or lead or join a Trail Ambassador hike in the Discover the Wissahickon series.

schedule.text: Volunteer service days and Discover the Wissahickon hikes are posted on the site. Listed for Oct 10, 2026: a Meadow Miler hike and a Saturday planting at Red Covered Bridge.

cost.text: Membership and donations are offered. Prices for hikes and service days were not checked.

first_step.how: Sign up for a volunteer service day through fow.org/volunteering, or come to the Saturday planting at Red Covered Bridge on Oct 10, 2026
first_step.basis: Service days and hikes are listed publicly, and the site gives a clear way to sign up

records.notes: The newest dated item is a news post dated Oct 8, 2026. The City list gives no address, so the office address and phone come from fow.org. The email green@fow.org comes from the City list because fow.org shows no email. Membership page: fow.org/membership-donations/membership/. Partner named on the site: Newrez presents the Discover the Wissahickon hike series; it is a company, not checked, and was dropped.
